turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Yeah, well, work actually sent me here. It's... I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks and work orders, and just basic follow-ups I promised people. It's gotten really bad, like, piled up so much that they said I needed to get this checked out before I lose my shot at moving up to a supervisor role. Which is frustrating because I've been doing maintenance for years, you know? Like, I can fix a boiler with my eyes closed. Last week, I was working on this HVAC unit over at the community center, and the coils were just completely shot—I told the guy, 'You can't just ignore the filter for three years.' People do that all the time, they just never change the filter and then wonder why the AC freezes over in July. Anyway, yeah, I just... I keep dropping the ball on the paperwork and the phone calls.

symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly states they keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups, which aligns with forgetfulness in daily activities.

turns.doctor_question: Have you struggled with these kinds of organizational problems and forgetfulness since you were a child, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, it's always been like this. I remember being exactly this way back in grade school, long before I had all this job pressure. My teachers always told my parents I was bright, but I was constantly misplacing my papers. I'd miss half the directions on assignments, and they always had to remind me to just finish my classwork. 

Like Mrs. Gable in fourth grade... she had this giant wooden desk, real solid oak. They don't make furniture like that for schools anymore, you know? Now it's all that cheap particle board that chips if you look at it funny. I actually had to fix a bunch of those cheap desks at the elementary school down on 5th street last month. The screws just strip right out of the laminate. You have to use wood glue and a bigger gauge screw if you want it to hold for more than a week, otherwise the kids just wiggle the tops right off again and it's a huge safety hazard. I keep telling the district they'd save money in the long run if they just bought solid wood the first time. 

But, uh, yeah, Mrs. Gable was always tapping on my desk telling me to get back to my worksheet because I'd completely forgotten what I was supposed to be doing.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes needing teachers to tap on his desk to get him back to his worksheet, indicating difficulty sustaining attention on tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports missing directions on assignments and needing reminders to finish his classwork.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states that he was 'constantly misplacing my papers' in grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient notes that he would have 'completely forgotten what I was supposed to be doing' during class activities.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech during the response, going on a long, loosely related tangent about school furniture, particle board, and carpentry before returning to the original topic.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel like you have an internal 'motor' that won't shut off, or do you find it hard to sit still for long periods of time?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have a motor going or anything. I can sit still just fine. I actually prefer sitting still sometimes, especially after a long day on my feet. Being a maintenance worker, you're always moving, up and down ladders, crawling under things. Like yesterday, I was under this sink at the municipal building, and the plumbing was an absolute nightmare. The guy before me used PVC glue on a threaded fitting, which is just... I mean, who does that? You're supposed to use Teflon tape. If you glue a threaded joint, you have to cut the whole pipe out if it ever leaks. And of course, it was leaking. It was this slow drip that had completely rotted out the bottom of the cabinet. I had to saw through the pipe in this tiny, cramped space, and my shoulders were just screaming. I've been meaning to get a new oscillating saw for jobs like that, the one I have has a battery that won't hold a charge for more than ten minutes. Lithium-ion batteries are great, but once they start going bad, they're useless. You might as well just throw them out. But they're so expensive to replace, you know? It's like fifty bucks just for the battery. 

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, no, I don't have a problem sitting down. I don't feel hyper or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about plumbing and tools before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states, 'I can sit still just fine' and 'I don't have a problem sitting down.'
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly denies feeling restless, stating, 'I don't feel hyper or anything like that.'
